item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00437","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C01","C20","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C01","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both are letters to congressional tax-committee chairmen in the same developing 1950 defense-tax program. They use the same progression: increased defense expenditures require prompt additional revenue; taxation should finance defense on a sound basis and restrain inflation; a specified tax measure should apply during 1950 and yield a stated annual amount at current income levels; the measure remains insufficient for longer-run needs, which will be assessed through later legislation; and a copy is sent to the chairman of the counterpart tax committee. C20 and C18 share parts of the defense-emergency fiscal predicate, but neither supplies comparably close tax-policy language or machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"we should finance our defense effort on a pay-as-you-go basis","parent_excerpt":"We must make every effort to finance the greatest possible amount of needed expenditures by taxation","explanation":"Both state the central policy that enlarged defense expenditures should be financed through taxation rather than deficits."},{"child_excerpt":"I believe the rates of the new tax should be designed to produce additional annual revenue of 4 billion dollars at current income levels.","parent_excerpt":"These adjustments in the pending tax bill would increase the Government's revenue, on a full year basis, by about $5 billion at present income levels.","explanation":"The child closely reuses the formulation of quantifying the proposed measure's annual revenue yield at current or present income levels."},{"child_excerpt":"Although the total amount of the expenditures which will ultimately be required for military security is necessarily uncertain, it will certainly exceed the yield of existing taxes augmented by such a profits tax. When the 1950 tax program has been completed with the enactment of this tax, we shall be in a position, early next year, to assess our needs for further tax legislation.","parent_excerpt":"Clearly, this will not meet our long-run revenue requirements. As an interim step, however, it will have a timely effect on tax revenues ... I expect to transmit further recommendations to the Congress concerning a more comprehensive tax program when we have additional information on the extent of our needs.","explanation":"Both characterize the immediate tax legislation as inadequate for uncertain longer-run defense needs and promise later recommendations once more information is available."},{"child_excerpt":"An adequate tax program is our strongest weapon in preventing inflation.","parent_excerpt":"It will serve to restrain inflationary forces generated by increased defense expenditures.","explanation":"Both make inflation control from defense spending a principal justification for increased taxation."},{"child_excerpt":"I am sending a copy of this letter to Senator George (Mr. Doughton).","parent_excerpt":"I am sending a copy of this letter to the Chairman of the Ways and Means Committee of the House of Representatives","explanation":"Both close by sending the same tax-policy letter to the chairman of the counterpart congressional revenue committee."}]}
